dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Yes, hello. This is Min-jun Tran. I'm calling about the storm drain in front of my building. Can you hear me okay? I have one bar here.
I can hear you fine, Mr. Tran. Go ahead, take your time.
Okay. So, last week, Tuesday or Wednesday, I first noticed it making a noise. A gurgling. Like somebody draining a bathtub, but out on the street. I thought, well, maybe it's nothing.
Mm-hm. A gurgling noise from the drain. Last Tuesday or Wednesday.
Right. Then came the nor'easter, last weekend, Saturday into Sunday. All that rain and the wind. And by Sunday afternoon the water was [line breaks up] over the curb and it would not go down.
I'm sorry, you broke up a little there. The water was over the curb and wouldn't go down?
Yes, over the curb. It sat there. And now, two days later, it's mostly gone but the drain still gurgles, and there is a smell coming up out of it. A sewer smell. Wicked bad, when you walk by.
A sewer smell coming up from the drain itself. Okay. And where are you located?
351 Kay Street. Up on the Hill, Historic Hill.
351 Kay Street. Let me write that down. Is the drain right in front of the building or at the corner?

Right in front. By the curb, next to where I put my trash barrel. And the sidewalk, you should see it. It's a sheet of mud and grit. All the silt came up and got left behind. I almost slipped yesterday and I'm seventy-something, I can't be falling.
That's no good. So mud and grit all over the sidewalk in front of 351. Is it blocking the whole walkway?

Most of it. You can walk on the side by the wall, but it's slick. And this isn't the first time, you know. Every time it rains hard, the thing backs up. I've been here a while and nobody ever comes to look.
I understand. I'll make sure this gets written up so a crew looks at it.
Good. Now, can I ask, is that a city drain or a state one? Because my landlord says maybe it's the state, and then nobody does anything. He says call the state, then the state says call the city.

Fair question. On Kay Street, those drains are generally the city's, since it's a city road. If it turns out to be something different, we'd be the ones to pass it along, so you don't have to chase it yourself.
Okay. That would be a relief. I'm tired of the runaround. I called nobody last week, I want to say that. This is my first call. But I'm telling you, it's been going on.

Understood. So let me read back what I have. Storm drain in front of 351 Kay Street, gurgling since about a week ago, backed up over the curb during the weekend storm, sewer odor, and mud and grit covering the sidewalk. Did I get that right?
Yes, that's it. You got all of it. Except the part where it keeps happening.
I'll add that it's a recurring problem. Do you want a call back when a crew has been out?
Yes, please. My number is four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-five-five.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-five-five. And that's Tran, T-R-A-N?
That's right. Min-jun Tran. Best time is in the afternoon. Mornings I'm usually out. Well, evenings too sometimes. But if I miss you, leave a message, please. And speak slow, my machine is old.
Will do. Afternoons, and I'll leave a clear message if I miss you.
Thank you. And, um, one more thing, sorry. Is there anything I should do in the meantime? About the smell? It comes in my window sometimes.

Keeping the window shut on that side is probably the easiest thing for now. And stay off the muddy part of the sidewalk if you can. If water comes up out of the drain into the street again, call us back right away and mention this report.

Okay. I will. You know, I would have called yesterday but I was home. My favorite program got moved to a different night, so I was sitting there waiting and then it wasn't even on. I missed the whole thing. Now it's on Thursdays, I think.
Oh, that's aggravating. They do that. Well, at least we've got the drain on the list now.
Yes. Thank you, Lorraine. Just please send somebody. I don't want to be calling again next week with the same story.
I hear you. It's logged, and someone from the department will be in touch. You have a good afternoon, Mr. Tran.
You too. Goodbye.
